source_snapshot.test_name_items: Next Boot Option - Under Power off
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Check each boot option can boot normal after setting
  none  : Do not change boot device order
  pxe   : Force PXE boot
  disk  : Force boot from default Hard-drive
  diag  : Force boot from Diagnostic Partition
  cdrom : Force boot from CD/DVD
  bios  : Force boot into BIOS Setup
  floppy: Force boot from Floppy/primary removable media
2. All the device should be set.
3. To check boot settings by ipmitool command: ipmitool chassis bootparam get 5
4. To check BMC WEB 'Operations' > 'Server power operations' > Boot Settings override should matached with ipmitool setting.
5. Enable one time boot should be selected after setting.
6. Reboot and check the booting in next boot.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Set ipmitool booting setting should be established successfully.
2. The one time boot should boot correctly after reboot.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" chassis status 2>&1; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" chassis bootdev pxe 2>&1; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" chassis power on 2>&1; sleep 120; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" chassis status 2>&1
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: verify the SUT is powered off, set the next-boot device (e.g. PXE), power it on, and confirm the boot option is applied.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: state-changing: sets next-boot device and powers the SUT on; confirm the desired boot device with the user first.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL identifies boot override plus power-on risk, but hardcodes only PXE, relies on a fixed 120-second sleep and final chassis status, exposes credentials and provides no independent proof that the host was initially off, booted PXE, consumed the one-time flag or preserved persistent order.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires true powered-off evidence, a supported per-option matrix, complete WebUI/IPMI readback, power-on approval, firmware/device evidence and one-time clear. V3.1 further distinguishes AC-present S5/soft-off from mechanical-off states and requires no automatic power-on after setting.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 913/2291 accepts the hardcoded command conditionally but does not define power-off authority/state, option applicability, actual destination markers, WebUI equivalence, clearing or recovery before another option.
historical_reviews.related_source_cases: The previous Under Booted case tests programming from a running host and is a separate initial-state path. Persistent boot order, wake-on-LAN and ordinary power-on tests cannot substitute for this matrix.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1075, Wistron-BMC-00204-V003 or 0670bf5f45a10127 draft exists in the invalidated run.
historical_reviews.v3: No V3 overlay exists for this exact case.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves the listed option and interface matrix; ED-34 treats power-state semantics, applicability and destinations as readiness inputs; ED-35 requires actual boot evidence beyond readback/status; ED-38 requires separate approval for override and power-on, recovery and no automatic retry.

original_test_intent: From a verified Project-defined powered-off state, confirm every supported one-time next-boot option can be programmed consistently through IPMI and BMC WebUI, takes effect on the subsequent approved power-on, clears after consumption and does not alter persistent boot order or power policy.
original_method: For each applicable option, independently establish the host's exact off state, baseline persistent order and override flags, confirm a safe bootable destination, set one one-time override, decode full IPMI and WebUI state, pause for explicit power-on approval, capture the selected firmware/device path, then verify consumption/clear and restore the approved off/normal state before continuing.
manual_activity: An engineer defines the exact powered-off state, option/destination matrix and separately approves each power-on. A human or independent observer confirms chassis/host state and non-OS destinations. Automation may set/read one override and collect the boot path, but cannot power on without confirmation, loop through options or issue the verdict.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT/BIOS identity and independent evidence for the required AC-present or other powered-off state
Applicable option map including `none`, IPMI/WebUI encodings and unsupported-option expectation
Trusted bootable PXE, disk, diagnostic, optical/removable and BIOS destinations with unique markers
Persistent boot order, power-restore policy and one-time flag baseline
Separate override and power-on approvals, maintenance window, console recovery, deadlines and final-power-state plan
Secure BMC credentials and preserved BMC/SEL/firmware/boot evidence collection
safety_requirements: Do not clear logs; preserve chassis power, boot parameters, persistent order, power policy and BMC audit/SEL before writes.
Verify the exact target and powered-off state independently; do not interpret one generic chassis-status line as sufficient if host, AC or transition state is ambiguous.
Do not expose passwords with `-P`, hardcode PXE, use untrusted boot targets or accept a fixed sleep/final power status as destination proof.
Obtain explicit approval first for the override and again for power-on. Do not combine the steps into an unattended sequence or automatically try the next option.
Stop on unexpected power transition, wrong destination, boot timeout, persistent flag/order change or lost console; preserve evidence and use the approved recovery path.
Verify consumption/clear and return to the specified normal/off state before another option; never use blind power cycle or persistent-order change as recovery.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target, exact off state, option mappings, destination safety, boot-flag decoder, persistent-order/power-policy baseline, approvals and recovery.
Set one approved one-time override, read complete IPMI/WebUI state and pause for distinct point-of-action power-on confirmation.
After approved power-on, collect firmware/console/device evidence and verify the selected path, one-time clear, persistent-order integrity and required final power state.
Stop without insecure credentials, fixed-sleep acceptance, untrusted media, automatic power/retry/matrix progression or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Define the authoritative powered-off state and approve the applicable option/interface/destination matrix.
Approve each override and power-on separately, with trusted media, recovery, deadlines and final-state expectations.
Review per-option setting, boot, clear and power-state evidence and issue formal verdicts.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Incomplete and unsafe as written: it hardcodes PXE, exposes the password, chains the state-changing power-on, waits a fixed time and only rechecks chassis status. It proves neither full matrix nor actual PXE boot or one-time consumption.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Build a one-option workflow only after the Project supplies exact power-state and destination inputs. Keep override write and power-on as separately confirmed actions and use firmware/device-specific evidence plus complete readback.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The seven options, `bootparam get 5`, WebUI/IPMI comparison, one-time selection, reboot wording, no Script, DeepSeek PXE/power-on command/risk and 10/10-minute estimates remain preserved; Review does not assume the fixed sleep or every legacy option is valid.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: For each applicable option, verify exact off state, set/read one override, obtain a separate power-on confirmation, prove the firmware destination and consumption, then restore the approved final state before continuing.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected BMC/IPMI/WebUI, BIOS and chassis power implementation with safe provisioned boot destinations.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC/IPMI/WebUI, BIOS/UEFI, chassis power controller, NIC/PXE and media versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform power-state semantics, IPMI boot-option mapping, BMC WebUI guide, BIOS policy and Project recovery SOP.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact off-state semantics, separate approvals, destination proof, clearing and final-state restoration while preserving the full option matrix.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Power status does not identify the boot path; testing only PXE does not cover other applicable options; an IPMI write does not automatically prove WebUI behavior.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Power state, option map, trusted destinations, secure method, approvals and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Power-on and redirected boot can start an unintended workload or network boot; absent media can strand the host; stale flags can affect later starts.

project_override_considerations: A Project may approve Redfish or vendor tools instead of ipmitool only with original IPMI/WebUI requirements, actual method, reason, approval and equivalent field mappings recorded. Passing an override does not prove omitted interfaces. Unsupported options require authoritative N/A justification rather than silent omission.
expected_evidence: Target/firmware identity, independent exact powered-off state, persistent boot order/power policy and full initial boot-parameter/WebUI baseline
Approved applicability and trusted option-to-destination matrix with separate override and power-on authorization timestamps
Per-option set/audit event, complete decoded readback and WebUI agreement before any power transition
Firmware/console/device-specific selected-path evidence and power-on/recovery timeline rather than a fixed sleep/status
Consumed/cleared override, unchanged persistent order/policy, restored final state, preserved logs, no retry and engineer-owned per-option verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Title, Procedure and Criteria consistently test next-boot programming from a powered-off SUT. The source says `reboot` after an off-state setup, but its functional intent is the subsequent boot/power-on; exact off-state and terminology are readiness clarifications, not irreconcilable purposes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The power-off next-boot objective is identifiable. Project/platform inputs can define the off state, supported options, safe destinations and recovery, so execution is pending rather than permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps PACKAGE but rejects unattended hardcoded PXE/power-on, fixed-sleep acceptance and status-only evidence; expands to a separately approved full matrix.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on hybrid control and adds exact off-state semantics, distinct write/power approvals and restoration to the required final state.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces command-exists sanity with off-state verification and per-option destination/consumption evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Preserves this power-off setup path separately from the preceding already-booted variant.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents an unattended PXE power-on and final chassis status from being reported as complete one-time boot coverage, and makes the initial/final power-state contract independently verifiable.
independent_technical_reasoning: A BMC may accept boot flags while the host is off, but the meaningful result appears only after a separately authorized power transition. Chassis state, firmware destination and flag consumption are distinct observations. Because source terminology does not define S5 versus other off states and legacy targets vary, execution needs an exact power-state contract and per-option evidence rather than a chained command and fixed delay.
